purpose: Bounded Fair Work Ombudsman record preserving two separate sales-worker episodes from commission-only underpayment through quitting, alternative employment, complaint, and reported full back-pay without inferring later recovery.

events.geography: Adelaide, South Australia; Longridge Group residential-property sales
events.date_precision: Employment period reported as 2011-2012; exact start and quit dates are not retained
events.denominator: One of two publicly described workers in the Longridge enforcement case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official Fair Work Ombudsman penalty release
events.missingness: Worker identity, exact alternative-employment date and quality, payment instrument, net receipt, household recovery, trust, recurrence, health, and later exit are not retained; the judgment records gross payment timing but not worker-signed receipt or adequacy
events.exposure: A 59-year-old sales worker with an MBA and 22 years of sales and marketing experience was hired after an advertisement promising potential earnings of $120,000 or more, but was paid $6,704 in commissions over ten months when minimum wages and entitlements should have totaled $20,013
events.alternatives_before_action: The worker quit after ten months and sought alternative employment; the public record does not identify the available offers, search effort, timing, or quality of the replacement work
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The commission-only arrangement produced a $13,309 gap against reported minimum wages and entitlements and forced financial dependence on the worker's wife during the underpayment period
events.choice_or_response: The worker quit, sought alternative employment, and complained to the Fair Work Ombudsman; the agency investigated and commenced legal proceedings after the employer refused to back-pay in full
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The employer controlled commission and wage payment; the worker controlled resignation and complaint; the Ombudsman and Federal Circuit Court controlled enforcement and penalty
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The company admitted breaches, was fined $29,790 across the case, and subsequently back-paid the two workers in full
events.remedy_receipt: The Federal Circuit Court judgment records that the amount due was paid in full, in two installments on 2 May 2013 and 1 October 2014; it does not provide a worker-signed receipt, net/tax or superannuation breakdown, or adequacy assessment
events.durability_followup: Alternative employment and reported full back-pay are observed, but later work, household security, trust, recurrence, health, and exit are unknown
events.immediate_outcome: Underpayment, resignation, alternative-employment response, enforcement, and reported full back-pay are documented for one worker
events.protected_outcome: Alternative work and reported restoration of the minimum-wage entitlement reduced the immediate employment and income exposure; durable security is not verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: The worker lost usable earnings during ten months of work, carried financial dependence and complaint effort, and lost the original employment relationship
events.cost_risk_transfer: The commission-only arrangement shifted wage and liquidity risk to the worker; enforcement and back-pay transferred formal liability back to the employer
events.later_outcome: The public record ends at alternative-employment pursuit and reported full back-pay, without later livelihood or trust follow-up
events.meaning_and_attribution: The Court and Ombudsman attribute the shortfall to unlawful commission-only payment and failure to apply the award; no worker-reported trust or meaning measure is retained
events.public_or_collective_response: Individual complaints and public enforcement are observed; no later collective or political action is reported
events.counterexample: Full institutional back-pay can follow a worker's exit and alternative-employment search while leaving the adequacy and durability of recovery unknown
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official Fair Work Ombudsman release dated 2015-02-03 plus Federal Circuit Court reasons, Fair Work Ombudsman v Longridge Group Pty Ltd [2015] FCCA 129, https://www.fairwork.gov.au/sites/default/files/migration/871/fair-work-ombudsman-v-longridge-group-pty-ltd-2015-fcca-129.pdf; the judgment records full payment in two installments but not worker-level signed receipt, adequacy, or later outcomes

events.geography: Adelaide, South Australia; Longridge Group residential-property sales
events.date_precision: Federal Circuit Court reasons identify the first installment date; worker identity is named in the judgment as Mr Moore
events.denominator: One named worker payment in the Longridge enforcement case; gross amount due was $20,013.60 before the commission offset described by the judgment
events.method: Structured extraction from the official Federal Circuit Court reasons
events.missingness: Net receipt, payment instrument, tax or superannuation treatment, adequacy, household recovery, later work, trust, recurrence, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: The worker's commission-only employment produced a court-calculated minimum-wage and entitlement shortfall; the judgment records the amount due was paid in full on 2 May 2013
events.alternatives_before_action: The worker had quit and sought alternative employment before the payment; replacement-job quality, duration, and later choices are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: A dated gross payment closes the formal monetary remedy for the identified shortfall; practical adequacy and residual loss are not measured
events.choice_or_response: Longridge paid the first installment after the underpayment and enforcement sequence; the worker's use of the money is not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The employer controlled payment; the worker controlled spending and any later work choices, none of which are linked in the public record
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The court record documents full payment of the calculated amount in an installment rather than a single lump sum
events.remedy_receipt: The judgment records payment in full on 2 May 2013, but does not provide a bank record, worker confirmation, net amount, or adequacy judgment
events.durability_followup: No later livelihood, household security, recurrence, trust, or exit record is retained
events.immediate_outcome: A worker-level payment date and gross amount are documented after resignation, alternative-employment search, complaint, and enforcement
events.protected_outcome: The formal wage shortfall was paid according to the court record; durable income security is not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: The worker carried the original wage and liquidity loss, complaint effort, and employment transition before payment
events.cost_risk_transfer: Payment transferred the adjudicated wage liability back to the employer, but residual timing and adequacy costs remain unknown
events.later_outcome: Payment is dated; later work, household recovery, trust, recurrence, and exit remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: The judgment attributes the shortfall to the unlawful payment arrangement; worker-reported meaning or trust is not observed
events.public_or_collective_response: Court enforcement is public; later individual or collective action is not linked
events.counterexample: A dated payment can close the formal remedy while leaving the worker's practical recovery and later choices unresolved
events.source_and_uncertainty: Fair Work Ombudsman v Longridge Group Pty Ltd [2015] FCCA 129, official court reasons; the judgment records gross payment timing but not independent receipt, adequacy, or later outcome

boundary: This ledger adds two separate worker episodes with observed underpayment, resignation, alternative-employment response, complaint, enforcement, and institutionally reported full back-pay. It does not establish independent receipt, adequacy, later livelihood, trust, recurrence, or exit.
storage_boundary: No worker identifiers beyond the public case description, payroll file, payment instrument, household record, or bulk archive is retained; only bounded official summary fields and explicitly open downstream arrows are represented.
